assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling made aryl amines, one of the most common motifs in pharmaceuticals and materials, accessible by a general, ligand-tunable reaction. It is a defining methodology advance in efficiency and scope for synthesis, with enormous routine use in industry and academia.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, broadly applicable amination with successive ligand generations and mechanistic work. Kosugi's 1983 aminostannane coupling was an important precursor but was tin-based and not general, so a two-person prize is the cleaner configuration, though precedence is a point to weigh.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation and ubiquitous use, including at process scale. Recognition is fully mature and arguably overdue; the Heck-Negishi-Suzuki prize in 2010 did not cover this chapter.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to acknowledge Kosugi's precursor or Migita-type tin chemistry in the citation.
Overlap with the C-H functionalization candidate through Hartwig.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a new mode of radical generation under mild conditions, enabling bond constructions that were hard to access thermally and reshaping late-stage functionalization and medicinal chemistry. Originality in synthetic design is high and impact is wide.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz independently established synthetic photoredox with Ru/Ir and later organic photocatalysts around 2008-2012; MacMillan's role is real but he is already a laureate (2021), and König and Fukuzumi have earlier photochemical antecedents. Credit is spread across many, so any three-person selection is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and now standard in industry; the field is mature enough but still evolving, and the long-term distinctive core versus general photochemistry is still being defined.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among at least seven named people with antecedent photochemistry.
Possible reluctance to recognize a field closely tied to a recent laureate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Catalytic C-H functionalization directly converts C-H bonds to new bonds with site selectivity, reducing step count and changing retrosynthetic logic. Ligand- and directing-group-controlled methods, especially for remote and sp3 C-H bonds, directly serve step-economy in complex molecule synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu pioneered ligand-accelerated and template-enabled Pd C-H activation across positions; Sanford developed Pd(II/IV) and related catalytic functionalizations. Hartwig (borylation) and others contributed, and the field is broad, so a clear subset is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation and numerous total-synthesis applications, though industrial adoption is less ubiquitous than cross-coupling and selectivity generality is still advancing.
uncertainties: Field is a broad family; a narrow credited set may omit decisive contributors (Bergman, Murai, Fagnou, Hartwig borylation).
Premature relative to cross-coupling in the eyes of some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides to give synthetic proteins and, with expressed protein ligation, semisynthetic proteins with modifications. It converted protein total synthesis from a stunt into a general tool and is a fine example of fundamental reaction design in chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson introduced NCL in 1994 and Muir extended it to expressed protein ligation; Danishefsky's contributions (glycoprotein synthesis) and others are valuable but more applied. Kent, Dawson, Muir is a coherent triple.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of consistent use, including synthetic erythropoietin and chromatin/histone studies; mature and stable.
uncertainties: Danishefsky, Brik and Liu allocations could be seen as omitted.
Impact is mostly within research tools rather than broad industrial practice.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts single bases without double-strand cleavage by combining deaminases with a programmable nickase, giving chemically precise genome modification with clear therapeutic relevance and first clinical successes. It is an elegant protein-chemistry construct.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab conceived and developed cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees, and Kondo and Nishida described an independent cytidine deaminase fusion. A single-person prize centered on Liu is the cleanest fit, though Kondo/Nishida precedence is a question.
assessment.maturity: About a decade old with clinical-stage validation, yet still young; the 2020 prize for CRISPR makes the timing and field placement debatable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers this chemistry rather than biology and whether it is premature after the 2020 CRISPR prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable carbenes overturned the view that carbenes are only transient species and gave N-heterocyclic carbenes as ligands and organocatalysts, underpinning modern ruthenium metathesis catalysts and many catalytic systems. Conceptual originality and broad reach in synthesis are high.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand isolated the first stable carbene (phosphinocarbene, 1988) and Arduengo the first crystalline NHC (1991), so these two are the decisive pair; Nolan, Rovis, Bode and others applied the chemistry.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of confirmation and wide use; timely or even late.
uncertainties: Whether the primary discovery or the later catalytic applications is the intended basis of a citation.
Bertrand versus Arduengo priority and the extent of Bertrand's main-group contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: ATRP delivers controlled radical polymerization with predetermined molecular weight and architectures from a metal-catalyzed halogen exchange, a synthetic-methodology advance with large materials impact.
assessment.attribution: Sawamoto/Kamigaito (Ru-catalyzed living radical polymerization) and Matyjaszewski (Cu-catalyzed ATRP) published almost simultaneously in 1995, so both are necessary; Wang's co-credit is plausible but less central.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of confirmation and industrial use; mature. RAFT is a close sibling that complicates a single-field prize.
uncertainties: Competition with RAFT for polymer recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation via PROTACs and molecular glues turns small molecules into inducers of ubiquitin-mediated degradation, creating a new modality for drugging proteins that were previously inaccessible. Many degraders are in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived the PROTAC concept, Ciulli developed VHL-based degraders and structure-guided design, and Handa/Ito's cereblon work on thalidomide is a separate decisive strand, so credit is complex.
assessment.maturity: Strong mechanistic confirmation but clinical validation is still emerging, so timing is possibly early.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with separate PROTAC and molecular glue parts needing different recognition.
Clinical efficacy not yet established at scale.
